entry.title: Standard Pricing Procedure Configuration for Inclusive Tax (Gross Pricing) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Publ
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community Experts,

We are trying to configure a standard Gross Pricing (Tax-Inclusive Sales / 含稅價銷售) pricing procedure in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, where the entered price already includes sales tax (e.g., 5% Output Tax), and the system needs to back-calculate the net value and tax amount automatically.

1. Business Scenario & Challenge

In our local market, products are quoted and sold at gross tax-inclusive prices. We need the pricing procedure in Sales Orders and Billing documents to:

  1. Accept the Gross Unit Price.

  2. Back-calculate the 5% tax amount (Output Tax).

  3. Determine the actual Net Value (un-taxed base amount).

  4. Present a final Total Value matching the gross total.

2. Current Findings & Key Discrepancy

  • We reviewed the SAP Community blog post titled "Tax-Included Sales Pricing in SAP S4HANA Cloud Public Edition" (and related KBA 3610515).

  • Critical Issue with Existing Article: In the first screenshot of the mentioned Community article, the calculated tax amount actually displays as ZERO (0.00). This renders the provided guide unhelpful and confusing for setting up a working tax-inclusive back-calculation mechanism.

  • Furthermore, KBA 3610515 (How to set Sales Tax Calculation Based on Tax Inclusive Amount) relies on a Custom Logic / BAdI workaround, rather than explaining how to achieve this via standard out-of-the-box SSCUI configuration.

3. Questions for the Community

  1. What is the official SAP-delivered standard pricing procedure setup for Gross Pricing (Tax-Inclusive Sales) in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition without using custom BAdIs?

  2. In SSCUI 101117, what are the exact step-by-step settings (From/To ranges, Subtotal, Reqt, CalTyp, BasVal, AcctKey) to ensure the tax amount is correctly calculated (and not zero) for:

    • Gross Base Price Step

    • Tax Condition Step (e.g., using TTX1 / ZTX1 with BasVal 11)

    • Net Value Step (e.g., using CalTyp 12)

    • Total Value Step (e.g., using CalTyp 4)

  3. Has anyone successfully deployed a standard gross pricing procedure in Public Cloud that passes clean net/tax values to Billing and DRC e-Invoicing?

Any detailed table setups, KBAs, or working examples from the community would be immensely appreciated!

entry.title: Enabling SIT-Based Proof of Delivery (POD) with Traditional Down Payment (FAZ / CBAO) in S/4HANA Clo
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community Experts,

We are seeking advice on how to integrate Stock-in-Transit (SIT) based Proof of Delivery (POD) with the traditional Down Payment Request process (FAZ / CBAO) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

1. Business Scenario

To comply with local tax and e-invoicing mandates via Document and Reporting Compliance (DRC), our system is configured to use the traditional Down Payment Request flow (Billing Type FAZ with Item Category CBAO). Simultaneously, our logistics process requires strict Stock-in-Transit (SIT) control, where inventory is transferred to SIT upon PGI and only cleared upon customer Proof of Delivery (POD) confirmation before issuing the final invoice.

2. Technical Limitations & Current Behavior

We encountered configuration blocks when attempting to set CBAO as POD-relevant:

  1. SSCUI 105504 (Define Proof of Delivery Relevance for Item Categories): The selection dropdown only allows standard item categories like TAN. Item Category CBAO is not available or supported for selection.

  2. SSCUI 107329 (Define POD Relevance for Order Types and Item Categories): The system only supports predefined order/item combinations such as Sales Order + CBXN or Sales Order + TAN. The combination Sales Order + CBAO cannot be maintained.

Current Behavior & Impact: When performing Post Goods Issue (PGI) on outbound deliveries containing CBAO items, the system executes an immediate direct Goods Issue (direct stock reduction) rather than posting to Stock in Transit (SIT, e.g., Movement Type 687).

Because CBAO cannot be flagged as POD-relevant in SSCUI 105504 / 107329, we are unable to utilize the standard SIT-based POD mechanism (moving from 687 SIT to 601 final issue upon POD confirmation) while fulfilling local DRC down payment requirements (FAZ / CBAO).

3. Questions for the Community

  1. Is there any standard solution or official workaround in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to enable SIT-based POD relevance for traditional down payment items (CBAO)?

  2. How are other companies handling logistics SIT controls (Movement Type 687 -> 601) alongside DRC-mandated traditional down payment requests (FAZ / CBAO)?

  3. Are there alternative order-to-cash workflows or FI-AR integration strategies recommended by SAP to bypass this item category restriction?

Any insights, KBAs, or architectural advice from the community would be greatly appreciated!

entry.title: How to Change the Useful Life of All Existing Fixed Assets to 3 Years in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public?
entry.content:
Hi,

We are using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for our India operations.

As part of a merger between two Indian companies, we have identified a difference in their fixed asset depreciation policies.

Business Scenario:

  • Company A is currently using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and has existing fixed assets with different useful lives (e.g., 5, 6, and 10 years).

  • Company B is using a legacy accounting system and follows a standard useful life of 3 years for all fixed assets.

  • As part of the merger, Company B's fixed assets will be migrated to the existing SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition system.

  • The business is also proposing to align all existing fixed assets of Company A with the 3-year useful life policy.

Business Requirement:

We would like to change the useful life of existing fixed assets to 3 years, while retaining their original acquisition values and previously posted accumulated depreciation.

Only the depreciation calculation should be revised based on the new useful life, subject to the approved effective date.

Queries:

  1. Is it possible to change the useful life of all existing fixed assets to 3 years in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition without changing the original acquisition values and previously posted depreciation?

  2. Can this requirement be achieved through asset class configuration, or must we update the useful life individually in each asset master?

  3. Is there any standard mass maintenance functionality or SAP-released API available to update the useful life of multiple existing fixed assets?

  4. Once the useful life is changed, will SAP automatically recalculate depreciation prospectively from the effective date, or will it calculate catch-up depreciation for previous periods?

  5. How will SAP handle assets that have already completed more than 3 years of useful life but still have a positive net book value?

  6. Since both companies are in India, are there any specific considerations for depreciation areas, accounting principles, or statutory reporting when implementing this change?

We would appreciate guidance on the recommended SAP standard approach, relevant configuration activities, Fiori applications, and any applicable SAP Notes or KBAs.

Thank you in advance for your support.

entry.title: Sending ZUGFeRD E-Invoices via Custom Middleware (Without DRC)
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

we are looking for a way to send ZUGFeRD e-invoices from SAP Public Cloud without using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (DRC).

Our goal is to automatically transfer billing documents to our own middleware, where they will be converted into ZUGFeRD format and subsequently sent to the customer.

The integration should only be triggered for specific customers.

We are currently considering using the EDI output channel and an outbound SOAP service to transfer the billing documents to our middleware. However, we are open to alternative approaches using SAP standard functionality.

The planned approach would be:

  1. Output Parameter Determination

    • Configure the output channel EDI for billing documents for specific customers only.

  2. Communication Arrangement

    • Use communication scenario SAP_COM_0223 (Sales with Buyers Integration).

    • Use the outbound service Customer Invoice – Send (B2B) (EDI_INVOICEREQUEST_OUT_SPRX).

  3. Communication System

    • Maintain the host URL of our middleware and configure the required authentication.

  4. Custom Fields

    • Our billing documents contain custom fields that also need to be transferred.

    • We are considering using the BAdI Modification of Header Fields in Customer Invoice SOAP Message (SD_BIL_EDI_INV_REQ_HEAD) to include these fields in the outbound message.

Our questions:

  • Is this a suitable approach to automatically transfer billing documents to an external system?

  • Is any additional configuration required to connect the EDI output in Output Parameter Determination with the outbound service?

  • Would you recommend a different or simpler approach to achieve this requirement using SAP standard functionality? We are not necessarily tied to EDI or SOAP.

We would appreciate any feedback, recommendations, or references to SAP documentation.

Kind Regards

Katharina

entry.title: Clarification on Asset Settlement Transaction Type 331 vs 336 in S/4HANA Public Cloud
entry.content:
Hello SAP Support Team,

We would like clarification regarding the determination of asset transaction types during settlement from an investment measure (WBS Element) to a fixed asset in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.

Scenario:

  • Costs were collected on a WBS Element and subsequently settled to a fixed asset.
  • The settlement posted to the asset using Transaction Type 331 (Acquisition Transfer from Investment Measure - Prior Year Acquisition).
  • As a result, the amount is reported under the Transfer category in Asset Accounting reports rather than under Additions/Acquisitions.
  • There was no actual asset transfer or disposal. The posting represents capitalization of investment costs to the asset.

Business Requirement: For audit and reporting purposes, the business would prefer such capitalizations to be reported under Additions rather than Transfers, where appropriate.

Questions:

  1. Is the determination of transaction type 331 vs 336 standard system behavior based on the fiscal year of the underlying costs?
  2. Is there any configuration, SSCUI, expert configuration, or extensibility option available in S/4HANA Public Cloud to derive 336 (Current-Year Acquisition) instead of 331 during settlement?
  3. If not configurable, what is SAP's recommended approach to report these postings as capital additions for audit purposes?

Example Asset: 20003751

We appreciate your guidance on the standard SAP behavior and any available options.

Thank you.

entry.title: Keep manual “Identification” value in payment media management after activating J78
entry.content:
Dear community;

We are working with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Until now, in the Manage Automatic Payments app, users created a payment parameter and manually filled in the “Identification” field with free text (date, currency, etc.) to identify the payment run. That text was then carried over to the payment media management app, where it was used to recognize it.

After activating scope item J78 (Advanced Cash Operations), what is entered in the parameter no longer reaches the payment media management app, and the field is now populated automatically with a value generated by SAP. Users have lost traceability of their payment runs.

Our questions are:

  1. Is there any configuration or parameter to deactivate the automatic population of this field by SAP and keep the text entered by the user?
  2. If not, is there a standard way to fill in a field when creating the payment proposal (reference, free text or other) so that it is visible later in the payment media management app?

Any experience or recommendation would be appreciated.

Thanks in advance.

entry.title: #CoE#GB Unexpected Quantity Change After Mass Update of Purchasing Info Records
entry.content:
Dear Experts,

We have encountered an issue while using the Mass Changes to Purchasing Info Records app and would appreciate your assistance in understanding the system behavior.

During the upload process, the value maintained in the upload file was:

  • Quantity: 100
  • Price: 1,105

After the upload was completed, the Purchasing Info Record was updated in the system as:

  • Quantity: 10
  • Price: 1,105

The quantity appears to have been changed from 100 to 10 automatically, while the price remained unchanged.

We have also reviewed the change logs and could not find any evidence that the record was modified by another user after the upload was completed.

Could you please help clarify the following points?

  1. Is there any standard SAP logic that could automatically convert or adjust the quantity during the upload process?
  2. Are there any unit of measure conversions, scale settings, or data interpretation rules that may cause the uploaded quantity of 100 to be stored as 10?
  3. Is this expected system behavior or a potential defect?
  4. Are there any logs, technical traces, or application logs that we can review to identify what happened during the upload?

The customer is concerned about the discrepancy between the uploaded data and the final result stored in the system. Therefore, we would appreciate your prompt investigation and clarification.

Thank you for your support.

Kind regards,

Ashley Hung
